Selected text, screenshots, videos, files and logs leave this server and are read by the Inkadra team. We add no name, email or instance URL. We remove GPS and other metadata from photos and videos from the device; PDFs leave whole, with their metadata. Check the preview. 0.title: The shooting calendar
0.text: On the Production board, one calendar for the whole project: the queue holds the frames and scenes of every storyboard. Day or week, like a calendar: blocks queue up by themselves. Drag a shot to the right time, or click it to add it at the end. With set plans, “Group by: Setup” puts the shots of each scene and day under their setup. The arrow beside the month folds the month and the queue; “Compact” and “Comfortable” change the height of the hours.

1.title: Storyboards and bars
1.text: The Storyboard filter shows the frames of one only; the coloured bar on the left of each block tells which storyboard it comes from. “Plan the whole scene” puts a scene in one block, even before it is drawn. A grey bar: the storyboard is not available, the label stays.

2.title: Move and stretch
2.text: Drag to reorder, Alt for a fixed time, the bottom edge for the length. Drop on a free date to create a shooting day; Ctrl+Z undoes the whole gesture. Drag on empty time to draw a block in 5-minute steps, then pick its type (keys 1–5). The Day view also has “Block” in the bar. With the keyboard, N adds a block after the selected one, or at the end of the day.

3.title: Move a whole day
3.text: Drag its heading to another column or to a date of the month: the blocks follow, and on a taken date the two days swap. Alt+←/→ or “Move to another date…” in the day.

4.title: Saves by itself
4.text: Every change is saved; Ctrl+Z undoes it, even across two days.

5.title: Calls
5.text: In the day’s Calls tab, choose who is called and write only the exceptions: another time or a pick-up.

6.title: Call sheet
6.text: Times with sunrise and sunset, locations, crew with phone numbers, the schedule with notes and what to bring. Pick the sections and print for the crew. Sunrise and sunset follow the project time zone: change it in Projects, the card’s ⋯ menu, “Type and time zone”. “Automatic” uses the device’s zone.

0.title: Draw the set
0.text: Lines, shapes, texts and measures from the bar at the bottom. Drag on empty space to select; click again to pick what lies underneath.

1.title: The library
1.text: Pick a category or search. Click a type and then the plan, or drag it there. Alt drops it free. The project kit gathers the lights and cameras of every plan.

2.title: Properties, elements, kit
2.text: What you select is set up in the right panel, and Lock keeps it where it is; Elements lists the plan by group, Kit counts the kit and the power per circuit, the first setup’s circuits serving them all.

3.title: Setups
3.text: One tab per setup: double-click it to rename it, the first one too. Under the tabs, a setup says what changed from the first, which can show behind it.

4.title: Walls and openings
4.text: Walls: click corner by corner, type a length and Enter, click the first corner to close the room. Openings: doors and windows go on a wall. With a scale, a room shows its size outside its walls.

5.title: Background
5.text: A floor plan or a photo under the drawing to trace over: move it, scale it, set its opacity and greys.

6.title: Move around the plan
6.text: Space and drag, the wheel or two fingers move the plan; Ctrl and the wheel or a pinch zoom it. With nothing selected the arrows move it, 0 fits it, at 100 %, + and − zoom.

1.text: Open a row: fields save automatically. Optionally link an account or character card.

2.text: Open “Paste from sheet” in the Crew toolbar. Review the preview before adding people. Headers and duplicates are skipped.

3.text: In the Schedule, Calls tab, choose who is called each day. The call sheet prints the crew, phone numbers and on-set contact, never for guests or clients.

0.text: The chip reads the scene’s number, INT or EXT and time of day from its card. Click it to open the scene.

1.text: Link an actor to a character and a camera to a storyboard frame: names, colours and lenses follow the cards. With nothing selected, link the plan to its location.

2.text: Set the time, and the date or a day of the shoot: the sun icons turn with them. North is set by hand.

3.title: Setups in the shot list
3.text: The shot list and the schedule show the setup of each shot, and the shot list can group shots by setup.

0.text: A PDF, PNG or JPEG of this setup or all of them, with the legend, kit, power and notes. On a phone it is in the setup menu.

2.text: Guests and readers open the plan in a view with pan and zoom, the setups, the legend and the PDF.

1.text: What exists stays visible and opens. Turn the module back on and everything is there.

1.text: Three levels, with the MB a minute for the resolutions chosen.

3.text: GPU only: resolutions not kept are prepared while someone watches, within the sessions the card can take.

4.title: Advanced
4.text: For experts: run the card test again, change live sessions and the values of each resolution. «Reset» goes back to the recommended value.

demo.limitToast: In the demo files go up to {{file}} and {{total}} in all.

encoder.offText: The server makes no copies: VIDEO_PROXIES is off or the worker has no ffmpeg.
encoder.cpuText: No usable graphics card · one copy at a time · slower
encoder.gpuText_one: The graphics card prepares the copies · one at a time
encoder.gpuText_other: The graphics card prepares the copies · {{count}} at a time

quality.title: Quality of the copies
quality.body: Applies to videos uploaded from now on. Estimates are for the resolutions chosen below.
quality.lightHelp: Takes little space. Fine for references and work-in-progress cuts.
quality.balancedHelp: A clean picture even with grain and movement.
quality.highHelp: For reviewing footage and colour grading.

rungs.title: Resolutions
rungs.480Help: For slow connections and phone data.
rungs.720Help: HD: the quality of cards on the board.
rungs.2160Help: Only for 4K originals. Takes a lot of space.
rungs.note: A video is never enlarged: a 720p original gets only 480p and 720p.

examples.title: One minute of original, and its copies

playable.label: Videos the browser already plays
playable.help: A 4K MP4 plays, but stalls on a slow connection.

encoding.title: Encoding
encoding.h264: H.264: plays in every browser and on every phone.
encoding.av1: This card can also encode AV1; Inkadra does not use it yet.

existing.title: Existing videos
existing.outdated_one: One video has copies made with the previous settings
existing.outdated_other: {{count}} videos have copies made with the previous settings
existing.upToDate: Video copies are already made with these settings
existing.help: Current copies stay until the new ones are ready.
existing.noRoom: About {{size}} more is needed: free some space before regenerating.
existing.first: New videos go first. You can close this page.
existing.dialogBody: The server makes the copies again with the settings of this page, one video at a time, after new uploads. Current copies stay until the new ones are ready; resolutions no longer chosen are removed.

live.title: Live playback
live.body: While the copies are made, or for resolutions you do not keep on disk, the graphics card converts the video as you watch.

reasons.no-gpu: Needs hardware encoding on the graphics card: on this server copies are made by the processor only.
reasons.too-slow: GPU too slow for real time (measured at start).
reasons.failed: The measurement at start failed: details in the server log.

live.upTo_one: Up to {{count}} person at once. Beyond that, viewers get the ready copies or the original.
live.upTo_other: Up to {{count}} people at once. Beyond that, viewers get the ready copies or the original.
live.zero: Sessions set to 0 in the advanced settings: live playback is off.
live.rungsHelp: For each resolution: keep it on disk, or make it only when someone watches.
live.never: Never live, they wait for the ready copies: ProRes, DNx, 4:2:2 video, interlaced, HDR, and vertical videos the card cannot handle in real time.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.intro: For people who know video encoding. Wrong values can give grainy or huge copies, or stuttering video: «Reset» brings each field back to the recommended value.
advanced.benchmarkRunningHelp: About 10 seconds. Copies being made slow down for a moment.
advanced.noGpu: No test: live playback needs the graphics card
advanced.noGpuHelp: Copies are made by the processor (libx264).
advanced.sessionsLabel: People who can watch live at once
advanced.overMeasured: More than measured: with many people at once videos may stutter, and the card slows down copies being made.
advanced.ratesHelp: Target: the average. Peak: the most in difficult scenes.
advanced.customNote: Some values were changed in the advanced settings.
